name: Rumtek Monastery
description: Seat of the Karmapa in Sikkim, renowned for its golden stupa and Tibetan art.
history: Originally built in the 16th century; rebuilt in the 20th century under the 16th Karmapa.
architecture: Traditional Tibetan monastic style with vibrant murals, courtyard, and prayer halls.
practices: Kagyu rituals, chants, and annual festivals including Tibetan New Year observances.

name: Pemayangtse Monastery
description: One of the oldest Nyingma monasteries, close to Pelling, famed for the Sangtok Pelri model.
history: Founded in the 17th century by Lhatsun Chempo, a revered Nyingma lama.
architecture: Wooden structures with intricate carvings and ancient murals.
practices: Nyingma rituals, meditative practices, and Cham dance during Losar.

name: Tashiding Monastery
description: Sacred site revered for Bhumchu festival and spiritual significance in Sikkim.
history: Dates back to 17th century; associated with Guru Padmasambhava's blessings.
architecture: Chortens, prayer flags, and hillside setting with panoramic views.
practices: Bhumchu water festival, prayers, and pilgrimages.
